text:
The man is likely to prevail. When the woman conveyed the house to him, he owned both the dominant and servient parcels, so the easement was extinguished by merger. It wasn't revived by his later warranty deed, which didn't grant it, or by the recorded path, and an implied easement fails because he never used the path while he owned both parcels. I know the team note says the answer is one of the two purchaser options, but I don't think either holds under the merger doctrine.

CONFIDENCE: 75
